findings.reason: the plan should cite and extend the existing derivation rather than describe a new one.
findings.text: the plan adds a session-scoped needs-you list without citing that `obligations(project, session)` (reckon/crew/obligations.py:782) and `_needs_you_runs` (reckon/cli.py:3229) already derive exactly that list, aged and state-worded

findings.reason: a second session-scoped duty projection drifts from `obligations()` and its MCP view, and the honest change is one line rendered from the existing owner, not a parallel composer.
findings.text: §2 proposes to compose the needs-you list in Python "beside the fleet partition in recovery.py", duplicating the session-scoped duty projection that already exists as `obligations(project, session)` (reckon/crew/obligations.py:782) and as `_needs_you_runs` (reckon/cli.py:3229); the live MCP view that "can return the same list" is already the `crew` view `obligations` (reckon/mcp.py:4331)

findings.reason: the forgotten list is the same projection with an age threshold and must extend `_fleet_counts`/`drain`, not fork the classification a second time.
findings.text: §5 derives the forgotten-run list "beside the fleet partition in recovery.py", but the fleet partition that already classifies each pointer — `_fleet_counts` (reckon/crew/recovery.py:10380) over `_watch_snapshot` (reckon/crew/recovery.py:10309), with `FLEET_UNPROMOTED_STATES` and session scoping — is the owner that already answers terminal-and-unpromoted and owns-session; `runs.drain(project, session=)` (reckon/crew/runs.py:1516) already reports the session's outstanding runs

findings.reason: collapsing the three composers onto one session-scoped duty projection removes the added surface and the drift between them.
findings.text: §2, §3 and §5 add three separate composers (needs-you line, drain line, forgotten list) over the same `_watch_snapshot`/classification machinery, each a shallow wrapper adding surface without hiding anything; the one deep module that should hide the record shape, the store and the join is the duty projection that already exists at `reckon/crew/obligations.py:782`

findings.reason: the line should render `drain()`'s result, or state why the owner cannot be extended.
findings.text: §3's drain line forwards to a drain condition already computed by `runs.drain(project, session=)` (reckon/crew/runs.py:1516) and surfaced as the `crew drain` command (reckon/cli.py:6043), without saying why that reader cannot carry the follower's line

findings.reason: the sections must account for the interface surface they add against the retirement of the existing obligations view and needs-you line.
findings.text: with public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23, §2 adds a `--remind` CLI option and a new MCP surface for the needs-you list, §5 adds a `reckon crew forgotten` command with `--hours`, and no section names what it retires or merges (the `obligations` MCP view and `_follower_end_line` already cover much of this surface) or states why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §2, §3 and §5 each add a separate composer over the same `_watch_snapshot`/classification machinery instead of one module hiding the record shape, the store and the join.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 re-implements the session-scoped duty projection owned by `reckon/crew/obligations.py:782 obligations()` and already present as `_needs_you_runs` (`reckon/cli.py:3229`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2 adds `--remind` and a needs-you list to the MCP surface, and §5 adds `reckon crew forgotten`, none of which names what it retires.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan adds needs-you, drain and forgotten machinery without citing the source that already derives each: obligations.py:782, cli.py:3229, runs.py:1516, or the obligations MCP view.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3's drain line is a thin layer over `runs.drain(project, session=)` with no statement of why that reader cannot carry it.
